cognition_match.developer_quote: HTTP status-code semantics: server-side 5xx responses to request-side detectable errors (invalid or missing parameters, non-existent resources, mode-inapplicable operations) are treated as defects by maintainers and repeatedly fixed
cognition_match.note: This candidate directly matches the documented blindspot pattern. Maintainers have repeatedly fixed similar issues (500->422 PRs 12049, 12040, 11878, 12262). The bug is that validation errors are not wrapped in ErrInvalidUserInput, causing HTTP 500 instead of 422.

verdicts.rationale: This is CONFIRMED as a true defect. The candidate correctly identifies that DELETE /batch/objects returns HTTP 500 for request-side validation failures (missing match.where and match.class parameters). Source code analysis confirms: (1) REST handler (handlers_batch_objects.go lines 185-187) explicitly checks for objects.ErrInvalidUserInput to return HTTP 422. (2) Validation function (batch_delete.go lines 127-137) returns plain errors.New() instead of wrapping in objects.ErrInvalidUserInput. (3) This mismatch causes request-side parameter validation failures to return HTTP 500 instead of 422. (4) Developer cognition explicitly states this pattern is a defect: 'HTTP status-code semantics: server-side 5xx responses to request-side detectable errors (invalid or missing parameters, non-existent resources, mode-inapplicable operations) are treated as defects by maintainers and repeatedly fixed' with multiple historical PR references. (5) The fix is straightforward: wrap validation errors in objects.ErrInvalidUserInput so the REST handler correctly returns HTTP 422. This is a clear violation of HTTP semantics and documented maintainer expectations.
